name: Liberal Socialism
summary: Liberal socialism holds that individual liberty and civil rights are compatible with, and are advanced by, the socialist goal of social equality. It pursues that goal through reform inside liberal-democratic institutions, a mixed economy of private and worker-controlled enterprise, and decentralised rather than centralised control. In Carlo Rosselli's formula, liberalism is the method and socialism the aim.
scope: The mainstream of the tradition as documented in the sources: John Stuart Mill's late cooperative socialism, the new-liberal and Rosselli strand (Rosselli, Hobhouse, Green, Bobbio and Calogero are named in the sources), centred on Rosselli's Socialismo liberale and Giustizia e Libertà. It excludes Marxist and Leninist socialism, and the market-liberal 'libertarian socialist' uses of the label. Many answers outside economics and political method are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Carlo Rosselli
keyFigures.role: Author of Liberal Socialism (1930) and co-founder of Giustizia e Libertà.

keyFigures.name: John Stuart Mill
keyFigures.role: Seminal source who argued that capitalist societies should gradually move to worker-controlled enterprises alongside private ones.

sources.usedFor: New liberalism, positive liberty, property as socially conditioned, welfare state.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Welfare provision is part of the liberal-socialist aim of freeing people from material necessity, so guaranteed health care fits the tradition.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not a topic of the founding texts; inferred from the commitment to reduce dependence and inequality within a reformist, liberal-democratic framework.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mill defends competition against socialist critics but sees monopoly and the subjection of labour to capital as real evils; adherents accept markets as a tool, not as a better judge than democratic institutions.

public-ownership.rationale: The tradition favours a mixed economy and rejects centralised state control; Rosselli-style strands accept socialising monopolies while others prefer cooperatives, so adherents split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Reducing material inequality through reform inside liberal democracy implies progressive taxation, though the sources give no specific rates.

unions-good.rationale: Worker organisation and association are central to the liberal-socialist route away from wage dependence.

property-fundamental.rationale: New liberals and Mill treat property as a social institution that may be reshaped when it entrenches unequal power; it is not an inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mill fears monopoly and favours state intervention in economic life where it protects liberty; liberal socialists back regulation of concentrated economic power.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is a means of securing real liberty; cutting it contradicts the synthesis of liberty and social justice.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mill expected capital to become the joint property of those who work with it, and economic democracy through worker-controlled enterprise sits in the core; adherents typically want it alongside private firms rather than universally.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the priority given to individual liberty and civil rights.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from Mill's harm-principle liberalism; the socialist side has no distinct view and adherents may differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; liberal free-speech instincts compete with egalitarian ones and adherents are split.

strong-leader.rationale: Rosselli fought fascism and held liberal democratic norms essential to socialism, so a leader bypassing institutions is rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberal socialists want a reformed, democratic state to secure social justice, not its abolition.

limit-guns.rationale: No stated position; inferred as split between liberal and egalitarian instincts.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on civil liberties, though Rosselli's circle endorsed armed anti-fascist action.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; adherents plausibly split between autonomy and concerns over exploitation.

decide-locally.rationale: Decentralised planning and self-management are favoured, so this is inferred for the political level.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from humanist emphasis on individual development and civil rights.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from Mill-style individuality and liberal pluralism; the sources do not discuss the family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic for the founders; inferred from commitment to individual liberty and equal civil rights.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on personal liberty and civil rights.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred from a secular, liberal political tradition; some adherents (e.g. Catholic liberal socialists) differ.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from commitment to equality and social justice; not addressed by the sources.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from Millian arguments that character is shaped by circumstance; not directly stated by liberal-socialist sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not a defining concern; adherents neither prize nor reject it.

gradual-change.rationale: Mill wanted gradual transition and Rosselli sought structural reforms within liberal institutions, though they also wanted deep change, so only mild agreement.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from universalist liberal and egalitarian outlook.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from internationalist, anti-nationalist outlook; not addressed in the sources used.

free-trade.rationale: Mill defended trade and competition, but adherents do not treat free trade as benefiting everyone, so split.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from the internationalist and anti-nationalist stance of anti-fascist liberal socialism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Rosselli organised volunteers for the Spanish Republic, urging that fascism be stopped abroad; modern adherents generally accept intervention for rights.

open-borders.rationale: No position found; adherents likely split between universalism and welfare-state concerns.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition is oriented to material emancipation, though Mill anticipated a stationary state.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from support for public action against collective problems.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No stated view; neither optimistic nor sceptical as a doctrine.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and not tied to any principle of the ideology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Rosselli rejected proletarian dictatorship and favoured reform, yet Giustizia e Libertà endorsed insurrection against fascist tyranny; adherents split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from the democratic emphasis on self-government and Mill's trust in citizens' own judgement.

central-planning.rationale: The ideology explicitly rejects centralised socialism, favouring decentralised planning and market-compatible worker enterprise.

socialized-markets.rationale: Mill's vision of competing cooperatives and the mixed economy of private and worker-controlled firms matches this, though liberal socialists do not require every firm to be socially owned.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not part of the liberal-socialist core; the sources opened do not address land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the aim of curbing entrenched unequal power through property; sources do not discuss inheritance directly.

basic-income.rationale: Compatible with freedom from material necessity but not a doctrine of the tradition; adherents differ.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Mill's openness to markets and competition suggests scepticism, though he allowed infant-industry exceptions.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Rejection of centralised state control and preference for decentralised, worker-run enterprise argues against state-directed investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mill and later liberal socialists favoured wide distribution of ownership and economic opportunity, including worker-held capital.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Mill envisaged cooperation replacing the wage relation but with markets and competition retained; abolishing money is not part of the tradition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from reformist acceptance of existing economic institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Rosselli opposed fascist corporatism; state-recognised bodies setting wages conflict with liberal freedom of association.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rosselli condemned the proletarian dictatorship as the dictatorship of one party and held liberal democracy to be essential.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from republican and egalitarian leanings, though constitutional monarchy is tolerated by some.

democracy-best.rationale: Liberal socialism takes liberal democracy as the method of socialism, and Mill treated democracy as a whole social organisation.

direct-votes.rationale: No stated position; representative institutions are assumed but participatory ideas appear.

workers-councils.rationale: The tradition prefers parliamentary liberal democracy as the method; councils as the basis of power are a Marxist-libertarian alternative it did not adopt, though Rosselli admired Catalan self-management late on.

right-to-secede.rationale: No stated position found; federalist sympathies pull one way, state unity the other.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inconsistent with equal civil rights and Mill's democratic emphasis on citizens' own judgement.

political-violence-never.rationale: Giustizia e Libertà called for insurgency against fascism, so adherents reject an absolute ban on political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from anti-fascist, liberal humanist outlook; war is not valorised.

separate-church-state.rationale: Secular liberal institutions are assumed, though the strictness of separation varies among adherents.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Incompatible with liberal pluralism and civil liberties.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Liberal socialists want public institutions for justice and security under democratic control.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from internationalist outlook; not addressed in sources.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Contrary to equal civil rights and to Rosselli's anti-nationalist anti-fascism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rosselli's book is a critique of Marxism and its determinism; liberal socialists see social conflict as real but not history's main driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The tradition stresses equal real opportunity and freedom from need rather than equal outcomes; adherents are split on how far to push redistribution.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are likely divided.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from universalist liberal outlook; Rosselli's federalism was European and political, not civilisational.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mill and new liberals reject radical individualism in favour of social sympathies and cooperation.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individual liberty and civil rights are central, so duties do not outrank rights.

limit-population.rationale: Mill supported voluntary limitation, but coercive or active state limits conflict with liberty.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The tradition aims at material emancipation through industrial society and rejects such pessimism.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; liberty favours freedom but egalitarian worries pull the other way.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from democratic self-government and rejection of technocratic control.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the priority on civil liberties.

restore-past-order.rationale: A progressive tradition; Rosselli sought a new socialist order, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The tradition is itself a deliberate ideological synthesis yet reformist and pragmatic; adherents split.

direct-action.rationale: Parliamentary liberalism is the method; direct action is accepted mainly against dictatorship.

means-match-ends.rationale: Rosselli's formula that liberalism is the method and socialism the aim expresses precisely that methods must embody the ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Utterly foreign to a tradition aimed at emancipation within modern society.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Mill's cooperative firms retain managers and specialised roles; abolition belongs to other socialisms.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Freedom from material necessity is a goal, but Mill and market-compatible schemes retain reward for work, so adherents are split on need as the ultimate criterion.

production-for-use.rationale: Adherents accept markets and competition so production for profit is not wholly rejected; ideal of production for need is not dominant.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rosselli criticised Marxism; Mill blamed subjection of labour to capital but not profit as theft.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rosselli explicitly rejected it as the dictatorship of a single party.

collective-farming.rationale: Mill favoured peasant proprietors and voluntary cooperatives, and liberal socialists reject coerced collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rosselli rejected Marxist determinism; the thesis of inevitable imperialist war is not part of liberal socialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Contradicts the welfare and redistributive aims of the tradition.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill's harm principle is a source, but liberal socialists also accept restrictions in the name of social justice, so only moderate agreement.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individual rights are primary, but associational freedoms and economic democracy involve collective rights, so adherents do not say rights are only individual.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from liberal emphasis on personal freedom, though anti-fascist war mobilisation complicates it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democratic voting is central; exit is no substitute for participation.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizens are members of a democratic community, not customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The tradition holds liberty needs political and economic autonomy and freedom from material necessity, as with Green, Hobhouse and Tawney.

media-academia-power.rationale: No stated view; inferred sceptical of the claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inconsistent with equal moral worth and egalitarian outlook.

organic-representation.rationale: Rosselli rejected fascist corporatism; adherents favour party-based liberal democracy.

total-state.rationale: Directly opposed to the liberal commitments and anti-fascism of the tradition.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rosselli's anti-fascism rejects the fascist myth of national rebirth.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Incompatible with democratic consent and the rule of law.

bound-labor.rationale: Incompatible with liberty and Mill's defence of free labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from Enlightenment liberal rationalism; no source addresses it.

universal-morality.rationale: Rosselli treated liberty as a universal value against Marxist relativism, but moral epistemology is not formally addressed.

single-common-good.rationale: Liberal pluralism accepts competing interests and negotiation among groups.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents divided.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Economic democracy and worker-controlled enterprises are named features, and Mill's associations elect removable managers.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from commitment to public provision of education.

economic-freedom.rationale: Liberal socialists accept some link of political and economic liberty but reject the market-only reading, so split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule of law and democratic accountability are central.

national-self-determination.rationale: Liberal tradition supports self-government of peoples, though adherents are wary of nationalism.

force-without-un.rationale: Liberal socialists favoured armed action against fascism but the sources say nothing on UN authorisation, so adherents are split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Liberal rationalism leans yes, but adherents include religious liberal socialists.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on welfare as a right.

class-collaboration.rationale: Mill sought partnership between capital and labour while Rosselli rejected class collaboration with fascism; adherents see conflict and cooperation as mixed.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Futurist destruction of cultural heritage is alien to liberal humanism.

dominated-front.rationale: No source links liberal socialism to anti-Western fronts; adherents have no shared view on it.

workers-nation.rationale: Internationalist and anti-nationalist outlook rejects organising on national lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Mill's equality of the sexes and civil-rights emphasis oppose it.

ban-interest.rationale: Mill's economics and market socialism accept interest and capital loans.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Race law is not discussed; Wikipedia's stress on individual liberty and civil rights alongside social equality clearly excludes legal segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rosselli rejected the Marxist view; liberal socialists treat the democratic state as a vehicle of reform.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from support for public action on environmental collective problems.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from liberal pluralism and respect for individuality.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy claim unsupported and contrary to liberal egalitarian outlook.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from democratic and pluralist commitments; not stated in the sources.

national-mission.rationale: Opposed to nationalist missions and aggressive state ideology.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian and civil-rights commitments; not documented in the sources opened.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not a doctrinal claim; adherents work within democratic institutions.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is not discussed; coercive limits on who may have children clearly conflict with the individual liberty and civil rights the doctrine puts first.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from rule-of-law and civil rights commitments.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The tradition expressly favours reform expanding the state's social role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not discussed; discouraging mixed marriages clearly conflicts with the equal civil rights and personal liberty the doctrine treats as core.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Wikipedia says liberal socialism joins individual liberty and civil rights to the goal of social equality; the SEP traces liberalism to Locke's view of people as naturally free and equal.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Rosselli attacked Third International doctrine; the question is a Marxist-Leninist one and liberal socialists do not hold it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources do not address settler states, and adherents are likely divided on the label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from equal civil rights, though pluralist views exist.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Contrary to liberal personal liberty and the harm principle.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from secular liberal tradition, though adherents differ.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Rosselli attacked Third International doctrine and favoured liberal institutions; a strengthened socialist state is contrary to that.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Consent is not addressed as such; Rosselli held the norms of liberal democracy essential to building socialism, which clearly implies government resting on popular consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Not discussed; forcing out a minority clearly conflicts with the civil rights and liberal-democratic framework the doctrine insists on.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Giustizia e Libertà called for insurrection against fascism, so adherents reject an absolute ban on initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Mill valued competition's role in innovation but rejected struggle as the engine of progress; cooperation also valued.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anti-fascists may favour restriction but liberty weighs the other way; adherents split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Mill and new liberals saw dependence of labour on capital as a threat to freedom even without abuse, aligning with non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Liberal democracy's institutions are the method; checks on power are assumed.

vanguard-party.rationale: Wikipedia says Rosselli rejected Leninist tactics that put organisational power over democratic procedure, and the dictatorship of the proletariat as a single party's dictatorship.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social justice and material equality favour priority to the worst off, though not exclusive.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; adherents plausibly divided between wider ownership and public housing stock.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Worker organisation is central; secret-ballot rules are not necessarily opposed but restriction is disfavoured.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Mill-style liberals weigh population but liberal socialists locate lasting poverty in institutions; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Representative election is the standard method; lottery is not a doctrine.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rosselli's anti-fascism defends legal protections even under pressure.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; Mill's market emphasis opposes while welfare commitments allow.

party-controls-media.rationale: Violates civil liberties; Fascist media control was a target of Rosselli.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not discussed; Rosselli's rejection of single-party dictatorship in favour of liberal democracy clearly excludes party command of the army.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; Marxist-derived demand not taken up.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Liberal tradition protects individual conscience of representatives.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and opposition to nationalism; the sources opened do not detail a federalist programme.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to the doctrine.

clerical-rule.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; rule by clerics clearly conflicts with the liberal-democratic method Rosselli made central.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rosselli supported democracies against fascism and rejected Leninist defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Contradicts Mill's liberty of expression and civil liberties.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from separation of powers and democratic alternation.

recall-officials.rationale: Representative democracy is assumed, but nothing in the sources endorses or rejects recall.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Coercive prohibition conflicts with liberty and liberal socialist reformism.

people-in-arms.rationale: Rosselli favoured volunteer armed resistance but a general replacement of professional armies is not part of the doctrine.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred from modernist, urban progressive outlook.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nothing in the sources bears on reunification; the principle of consent cuts both ways.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from respect for education; Rosselli's movement was intellectual.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Liberal universalism leans against strict relativism while pluralism leans to it; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Humanist liberal tradition opposes it; inferred from civil-rights emphasis.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from education and equality commitments.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from Millian liberty; some egalitarian dissent.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Liberty of conscience favours; equal law disfavours; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's On Liberty is the source; individuality and experiments in living are explicitly valued.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The sources do not address sovereign debt; egalitarian and market-respecting instincts conflict.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: An anti-colonial claim the sources do not address; adherents have no shared view.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the democratic method and consent principles; the sources opened do not describe a constituent-assembly programme.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberty is both goal and method, so growth cannot justify suspending freedoms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian and social-justice commitments extended abroad.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional design of the presidency is not addressed in the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not addressed in the sources, so no committed answer is available.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and peaceful settlement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Mill and new liberals treat property as legitimate according to its social function, leaving it open to reform.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Rosselli attacked Stalinism but the state-capitalist thesis is a specific Marxist analysis; many liberal socialists regard the USSR as non-socialist for lacking liberty, others do not use that label.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from anti-fascist internationalism and collective security.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from self-determination and consent principles.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Secular tendencies favour curbs on privilege but religious liberty disfavours state subordination; split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss the head of state's role, and republican and monarchical adherents differ.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from consent and self-determination principles.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No source treats regional autonomy under a larger state, so adherents have no settled view.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Not discussed; a sacred, divinely descended ruler is clearly incompatible with the liberal-democratic framework the doctrine requires.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Redistribution through progressive taxation is part of reducing inequality.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on opportunity and education; the sources opened do not state it directly.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Directly opposed to rule of law and liberal constitutionalism.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a concern of the tradition; no principle points either way.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader cults are not discussed directly, but Wikipedia calls anti-fascism an important component of Rosselli's liberal socialism, which clearly implies rejecting one.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law presumptions are not addressed; equality and child-welfare considerations conflict.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine incompatible with the tradition's liberal pluralism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Mill favoured peasant proprietorship in some settings but not confiscation; split.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; universalism favours return but adherents give no common position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism is not discussed; inferred from the doctrine's liberal internationalism, though Rosselli also drew on Mazzini's national tradition.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; punishing apostasy clearly violates the individual liberty, including religious freedom, that liberal socialism keeps from liberalism.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not discussed; a legal dress code for women clearly conflicts with the individual liberty the doctrine treats as both goal and method.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed beyond European federalism; split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from civic rather than ethnic basis.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and pluralist and unitary civic views both occur among adherents.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the civil-rights, universal-citizenship approach.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rosselli criticised Marxist economic determinism and stressed moral and voluntary agency.

ban-cartels.rationale: Mill saw monopoly as a greater threat than competition and economic democracy opposes concentrated power.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberal democracy includes rights protected from majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from commitment to equality; adherents may prefer persuasion to quotas.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from welfare commitments and internationalism.

moral-incentives.rationale: Market-compatible tradition keeps material incentives, though Mill valued social sympathies.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Rosselli favoured armed action only against dictatorship and rejected Leninist vanguardism; foquismo is not his doctrine.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mill and liberal egalitarians attacked hereditary privilege as incompatible with equal citizenship.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inconsistent with equality and self-government as the tradition now understands them.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from commitment to substantive equality.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not part of the tradition's stated positions; adherents likely divide.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Reformist rather than collapse-oriented: it favours progressive reform within capitalism rather than its abolition.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Rosselli and the new liberals stressed liberty and anti-fascist internationalism; cultivating influence over a predecessor empire fits imperial nationalism, which the tradition opposes. Inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Mill defended competition and exchange, and liberal socialists seek reform within open liberal-democratic economies, not autarkic delinking. Inferred from that.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The tradition treats workers as a common class to be raised by reform and cooperation, not a Leninist split between exploited and complicit workers. Inferred from its rejection of Marxist-Leninist theory.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Liberal socialism pairs civil rights and equality with property seen as socially conditioned, so it would back anti-discrimination law over an absolute right to refuse. Inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberalism as method means civil liberties secured against majorities and one-party rule, which Rosselli defended against fascism; inferred that written entrenched guarantees fit.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from its liberal commitment to self-determination; not addressed in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-democratic method and Rosselli's republicanism against fascism.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from liberal democracy's majority rule bounded by individual rights, rather than a consent veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Rosselli's Giustizia e Libertà resisted the Fascist regime, and liberalism supports resisting rulers who break constitutional limits.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from liberalism as method, meaning parliamentary democratic institutions.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from Mill's tradition of extending utility to suffering; not addressed in the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from mainstream liberal acceptance of animal use with limits on suffering.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: New liberals stress social rights, not paternal duty; adherents are split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Rosselli led active anti-fascist political resistance, and liberal socialism treats participation as central.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from liberalism's trust in individual judgment; not stated in the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of Marxist class theory.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between dependency and liberal development views.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from liberal equal citizenship and internationalism.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from Rosselli's rejection of Soviet direction and support for national democratic paths.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian and internationalist outlook.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from its liberal internationalism and opposition to nationalist militarism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from liberal equal citizenship, which opposes descent-based political rank.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Rosselli founded the anti-fascist Giustizia e Libertà, making anti-fascism foundational to the tradition.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Rosselli's liberal socialism opposed both fascist and Soviet-style dictatorship, though the sources do not speak of equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from liberal anti-slavery tradition and mainstream history.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Liberal commitments to memory and to redress conflict; adherents are split.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from liberal universalism of equal concern.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred as split between equal-protection principles and attention to gendered power.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the universalism of liberal rights and democratic institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-democratic rejection of military rule.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the socialist aim of social equality; not addressed directly.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; its liberal stress on individual choice and its welfare aims pull in different directions, so inferred as neutral.

office-by-exam.rationale: Mill favoured competitive examination for the civil service while the tradition prizes democratic accountability; inferred as split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to open exchange and the reformist, non-nationalising mixed economy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Mill and the liberal strand defend individual liberty in private life against legal and social coercion, which covers freedom to end a marriage.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Liberal socialists work within representative institutions where representatives use their judgment (Mill's view); inferred from that.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the welfare-state and new-liberal commitment to social provision against material insecurity.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Mill favoured taxing unearned land rent but not abolishing private holding, and the tradition is reformist; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Rosselli and the liberal strand hold parliamentary government and the rule of law as the necessary method, which includes legislative control of public money.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to pluralism and minority rights.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from liberal openness and internationalism; the founding texts do not address it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: New liberals back equality of opportunity but liberal adherents divide over judging by outcome; inferred as split.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Mill criticised the pursuit of wealth but liberal socialists respect individual choice; inferred as split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from liberal preference for law and non-violent method; Giustizia e Libertà itself backed armed anti-fascist resistance, which tempers it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Rosselli's rejection of dictatorship and the liberal commitment to self-determination rule out forced control of allies.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: Rosselli and the new liberals worried about concentrated economic power distorting democracy and freedom.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: liberal commitments to open society and civil liberties cut against restricting funding of media and universities.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the tradition supports pronatalist policy, and its liberal internationalism is open to immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: liberal freedom of movement and property rights make residency-based restrictions unattractive.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: social equality and freedom from want suggest support for a right to work, though liberal socialists differ on the method.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalism favours democracy and expects peace to follow from it.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: liberal socialists work through constitutional order and the rule of law, so they reject it as a general principle.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalism supports collective action to protect rights, so a blanket ban is rejected.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: Mill and Rosselli backed workers' associations and unions, but the sources don't address union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Liberal socialism is rooted in individual liberty, equal rights and pluralism, which exclude targeting a minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: liberalism's emphasis on equal civil rights and Mill's defence of women's equality favour reform, not abolition, of marriage law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: liberal belief in accountable government and civil rights supports a right of access to public information.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: liberal socialists favour open exchange and decentralised enterprise, but not localism as a principle.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: Rosselli's Giustizia e Libertà was an organised movement and the tradition works through parties and parliament.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalism and rights protections point to constitutional courts being checked by international norms.

religious-nation.rationale: Liberal commitments to freedom of conscience and equal citizenship rule out defining the nation by religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from liberal-socialist commitment to equality under law and national self-determination, which excludes ritual submission between states.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian aim of reducing inequality, which favours sharing by need, though Rosselli's federalism favours decentralised control.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Liberal socialists want a mixed economy of private and worker-controlled enterprise, so the means of production are not wholly held in common.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rosselli rejected proletarian dictatorship and fought fascism, but liberal socialists stress change by persuasion within democratic methods; I treat the choice as split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Mill's competition and the mixed economy of private and cooperative enterprise, and decentralised control, fit mixed providers inside a publicly funded system.

religion-illusion.rationale: Liberals defend freedom of belief and treat religion as a lasting private matter; I infer disagreement that it is a mere illusion that fades.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Mill defended competition and held capitalist societies as a stage toward associations; new liberals credit markets with wealth creation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Liberal socialists pursue equality by rights and reform within liberal-democratic institutions rather than by transforming the economic system as a whole.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the liberal emphasis on individual choice and family freedom, which favours optional public services over public replacement of domestic work.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; liberal principles of free expression and pluralism imply that language purges are illegitimate.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to the rule of law and keeping agreements, matching its answer on colonial treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Mill favoured voluntary cooperative associations, but liberal socialists keep the state, markets and private property alongside them.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from liberal protection of minority rights and equality before the law, which excludes steering majority settlement into minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rosselli rejected both Marxism and laissez-faire capitalism, defining liberal socialism as a third course combining liberty and equality.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from liberal universalism and equal individual rights, which sit badly with ranking peoples' claims by ancestry or religion.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is incompatible with the liberal-socialist anti-fascist tradition of Rosselli and Giustizia e Libertà.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Criminalising consensual private conduct contradicts the civil liberties at the core of liberal socialism, following Mill's harm principle.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Rosselli's liberalism-as-method rejects one-party dictatorship and the suppression of opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Freedom of conscience and expression are core liberal commitments the tradition inherits from Mill.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Liberal socialism's equality and self-government principles condemn exploiting subject territories for the ruling country's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: a secular, individual-rights tradition does not accept religious obligations as binding politics, though it supports resisting invasion.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Legitimacy comes from democratic consent, not religious law, and rejecting force against elected governments is core to the liberal method.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Decentralised control and worker associations imply wide participation, though the tradition works within representative institutions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: the tradition links liberty and social equality, but it predates and does not use intersectional analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from liberal protection of individual self-determination and equal rights; the founding texts do not address it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Mill-style personal autonomy over one's own life, with safeguards; the founding texts do not address it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Rosselli placed liberal socialism on the left as a form of socialism, rather than transcending the divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: Mill's cooperative case criticises wage labour's subjection of workers to capital, though not in Marx's alienation vocabulary.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Pluralism and equal rights for all citizens are core liberal commitments, which reject the claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority rests on consent and democratic institutions, not divine source, in the liberal tradition.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: secular state neutrality and individual freedom of conscience pull in opposite directions, and liberals are split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from liberal protection of individual rights and access to courts; the founding texts do not address it.

social-market-economy.rationale: The mixed economy of private and cooperative enterprise with welfare provision, as in Mill and the new liberals, matches this.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Rosselli championed armed anti-fascist resistance, and the tradition accepts defensive force within liberal states.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the equality aim of the tradition, which rejects letting inequality persist to be removed later.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: Rosselli backed anti-fascist intervention, so the tradition is split between neutrality and alignment against tyranny.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inherited office contradicts the liberal-democratic institutions the tradition works within and its equal-citizenship aim.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Mill's endorsement of cooperative, worker-controlled enterprise in a mixed economy.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the reformist, egalitarian aim of social equality that places national choice over lender conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Liberal socialism extends liberal civil and political rights to all, and wealth-based voting would defeat its egalitarian aim.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not a theme of Rosselli or Mill's economics; inferred from the shared opposition to unjustified hierarchy in its egalitarian liberalism.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept; liberal socialists reject Marxist determinism yet accept that markets can shape social life, so adherents are split. Inferred, not stated.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the claim that liberty must be made real through greater social equality, which includes access to means of expression.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law under fixed, general rules is a core liberal commitment that liberal socialism keeps as its method.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial limits on citizenship contradict the liberal equality of rights that the tradition keeps at its core.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed historically; inferred from the commitment to democratic participation within liberal institutions.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic accountability and publicity of government.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Legal limits on marriage by religion violate the individual liberty and freedom of conscience at the core of liberalism.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Singling out people by religion offends the equal respect and tolerance liberalism upholds.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Rosselli and Mill defended representative liberal institutions while valuing decentralised participation; lotteries are not discussed, so adherents are split, inferred from the principles.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The tradition is secular and rests on freedom of conscience and reasoned reform, so it favours updating inherited doctrine over fixed authority; inferred, not addressed in the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Mill and the new liberals treat subjection of labour to capital and unequal property as threats to real freedom, which is why they seek wider ownership and equality of means.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; inferred from its commitment to equal civil rights and individual liberty.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Liberal socialists hold to liberal neutrality and freedom of conscience, and Rosselli rejected state coercion of belief, so state-promoted unbelief is out.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The tradition works inside the liberal-democratic state and rule of law; abolition is not part of it (inferred from its reformism).

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; liberal-democratic constitutionalism could favour either consociational guarantees or majority rule with individual rights.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The new liberals and Rosselli argue that the state must guarantee welfare and material freedom, not leave the poor to charity.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; adherents could value renewal or experience equally.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; liberal socialists favour representative parliamentary democracy and some decentralised participation, so adherents are split on delegable voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: An anachronistic question for the tradition; no stated position, and priorities lean to present social reform.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal commitment to equal rights, though the state does not govern religious bodies' internal rules.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from Mill's equality of the sexes and the tradition's equal individual rights.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Equal civil and political rights are central to the liberal half of the tradition; the sources do not address residents' votes, so this is inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the aim of social equality through reform inside liberal-democratic institutions; rent caps are not discussed in the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: The sources say nothing on intellectual property, and liberal-socialist reformers could favour either reform or retention.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Rosselli's anti-fascism and the liberty-first method, which are opposed to regimented, drilled national youth organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the tradition's anti-militarist, internationalist liberal outlook.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the tradition's internationalist liberal outlook and its preference for national self-determination.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the tradition's commitment to civil rights and historical truth in a liberal democracy.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Mill's late socialism holds that the evil lies in the subjection of labour to capital and expects returns to follow work in cooperative associations.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not stated in the sources; inferred because Rosselli's Giustizia e Libertà resisted fascism by force, so absolute non-resistance does not fit.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the liberal, individualist and anti-nationalist outlook of the tradition.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; liberal socialists have no collective position on this feminist-theory question.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; liberal socialists have no collective position on this feminist-theory question.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the secular liberal rejection of nationalist cults, which Rosselli opposed in fascism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to pluralism and secular politics, which treats politics as compromise rather than holy war.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the tradition has no position on diaspora policy.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of liberal institutions and civil rights as the method of reform, rather than cultural renewal.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; religion is a matter of individual conscience for the tradition, and adherents are split.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to the equal rights and freedom of every person, which gives a mild yes.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from liberal universal civil rights and equality, which reject ethnic privilege in economic life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the liberal preference for individual rights and decentralised, not ethnic, territorial units.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to civil liberties and pluralism: Rosselli rejected party-state dictatorship, so unions must stay free of state and party.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from Mill's and Rosselli's emphasis on workers' self-government and cooperative control; real worker agency is what separates this socialism from state ownership.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the reformist mixed economy and welfare aims, which keep basic services under public provision.

second-chamber.rationale: Liberal-socialist texts do not address legislative design; adherents accept both unicameral and bicameral liberal-democratic systems.

municipal-property.rationale: The tradition favours cooperative and worker-controlled enterprise alongside private and public ownership, but does not single out municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Rosselli's liberal socialism favoured decentralisation and autonomies, but the sources do not discuss confederal structures with non-binding delegates.

family-wage.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; welfare-minded adherents would support family support but liberal socialists also stress individual rights and equal pay.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: No stated view; liberal regulation favours safety while welfare-minded reformers favour access, so adherents are split.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: No stated view; the tradition backs public research and health but does not address life-extension specifically.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Civil liberties favour private transactions, but reformist egalitarians want tax enforcement and state oversight of finance; adherents split.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to freedom of expression and privacy as civil rights.

person-over-state.rationale: The liberal half of the synthesis holds that the individual is the end of politics and may not be sacrificed to the collective; Rosselli rejected totalitarian subordination of the person.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The sources say nothing on spiritual nature; Rosselli and Mill held rich views of human development but the tradition is secular and mixed.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split between centralised parliamentary sovereignty and Rosselli's autonomist, regional decentralisation.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition has no stated position on genetic engineering, and adherents are split.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and no principle of the tradition points either way.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to equal individual rights and the socialist concern with class; political organisation along racial lines conflicts with both.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from the universalist, individual-rights outlook of liberalism, which treats racial pride as no basis for politics.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from Rosselli's anti-fascism and liberal internationalism, which condemned aggressive war, though adherents have accepted interventions to defend liberty.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Liberal socialism builds on individual liberty and civil rights, and Rosselli opposed nationalist and fascist definitions of the people; inferred, not stated in the sources.

communal-electorates.rationale: Liberal socialism favours equal individual citizenship in common institutions, so separate religious electorates are inferred to be rejected.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Rosselli fought nationalist fascism and the tradition is internationalist and sceptical of nationalist conspiracy narratives; inferred from that stance.

free-public-college.rationale: Equality of opportunity is central to the new-liberal and Rosselli strand, and free public higher education follows from it, though the sources do not name tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Liberal socialists accept both market-based corrective taxes and regulation; the sources do not address it and adherents plausibly split.

future-generations.rationale: Mill's Principles envisaged a stationary state that preserves nature, so a duty to hand on the Earth undamaged is inferred from that passage and liberal concern for later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Liberal socialism stresses individual rather than group outlook, though Mill argued for women's equality; no stated view on distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Rosselli's European federalism and the liberal-internationalist tradition favour disarmament by agreement; inferred, not stated in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Liberalism's commitment to public accountability implies open diplomacy; inferred from the liberal method, not stated in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Liberal socialists favour a mixed economy but the sources say nothing about capital controls, and liberal and socialist halves point opposite ways.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on rule of law and liberal-democratic institutions, which imply a lawful state monopoly on force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: Rosselli fought in the Great War and organised armed anti-fascist resistance, so a blanket duty to refuse is unlikely.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the aim of advancing workers' collective strength within a liberal framework, which the sources do not discuss directly.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the new-liberal and socialist aim of reducing inequality through reform inside the market economy.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred as split: the liberal side favours rule-bound government, the socialist side favours room for public investment.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's concern with social equality, which the sources do not extend to international economic rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Rosselli's formula makes liberal method the means to socialism, and the tradition rejects revolutionary dismantling of democratic institutions.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from Mill's treatment of cooperative associations as arrangements to be tried and from the tradition's preference for decentralised, mixed-economy forms.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic for most of the tradition; inferred as split between liberal valuation of resources and socialist objection to commodification.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred from the liberal emphasis on individual liberty and the tradition's opposition to fascist nationalism.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the aim of equal opportunity and wider social equality, not from any stated position on loan cancellation.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred as split: the sources do not address regional exploitation, and the tradition emphasises individual rights over structural regional analysis.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the liberal grounding of rights in universal human dignity; the sources do not discuss redesigning human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from liberal concern for a free and plural press combined with public provision of civic goods.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The sources are silent on religion's truth claims; liberal neutrality suggests indifference.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the mixed economy and cooperative associations the tradition favours, which extend naturally to farm cooperatives and public support.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic for most thinkers in the tradition and not addressed; adherents later split between multilateral disarmament and deterrence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Rosselli's movement was cross-class and liberal socialists often worked inside broader parties, so adherents are split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the liberal insistence on individual rights and bodily integrity; the sources do not mention FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to equal legal rights, with Mill a well-known advocate of women's equality.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no position follows from the principles.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: the tradition accepts state regulation of markets in the public interest, over reliance on private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic method, which rests lawmaking on elected representation.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from Rosselli's view of liberty as the method that must not be sacrificed to substantive aims.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to rule of law and individual justice, which favours judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; liberal pluralism and civic integration pull in different directions.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: the tradition backs worker organisation within liberal rights, so it would not accept a ban on union-security arrangements, though individual freedom of association gives some pull the other way.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to equal civil and political rights; adherents would worry about ID rules excluding poorer citizens, though the tradition does not address the issue.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from liberalism's religious neutrality and equal civil rights, which the liberal-socialist tradition inherits.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Rosselli and Mill treat liberalism as a method; democracy means more than procedure, since the socialist aim of social equality is part of what makes government legitimate.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to individual freedom of conduct and the equal standing of women.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Cutting communications conflicts with the civil liberties of expression and information that liberal socialism holds as non-negotiable.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the tradition accepts guaranteed minimum support but favours a welfare state and social provision over replacing it with a market-style cash scheme.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal civil and political rights are the liberal core of the tradition; Mill himself argued for women's suffrage.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: a secular, liberal outlook may criticise some religious institutions, but the tradition does not blame religion as a major cause of women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from liberal egalitarianism and its modern reformist adherents; the founding texts do not discuss race categories.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the reformist welfare-state commitment to social equality pursued through public institutions.

missingStatements.text: Parliamentary democracy and civil liberties are the necessary method for reaching socialism, not obstacles to it.
missingStatements.rationale: Rosselli's formula that liberalism is the method and socialism the aim, and his rejection of one-party dictatorship, make this the core claim.

missingStatements.text: Workers' associations should gradually replace the wage relationship between employer and employee.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill expected wage labour to give way to partnership and cooperative associations, arguing the evil lies in the subjection of labour to capital.

notes: The label overlaps with social liberalism and social democracy, and several answers could shift toward those. Italian strands (Rosselli, Calogero, Bobbio) and Mill's cooperativism differ on public ownership. Rosselli's primary text was not itself opened (only Wikipedia's account of it).
